adaptation_structure.task: AI prompts teacher request for activity examples and modifications according to child ability level
adaptation_structure.output: Let me know if you would like activity examples, modification of activity by child ability level (low, middle, high)

activity_examples.task: Respond to teacher request to provide multiple examples of phonemes, graphemes, letter-sound patterns, words, sentences of the targeted skills
activity_examples.output: Provide detailed lists of phonemes, graphemes, letter-sound patterns, words, sentences of the targeted skills that teachers could use in their activities

ability_level_modifications.task: Respond to teacher request for a modified teacher script in which the activity changes according to teacher request of Low, Middle, or High child level ability
ability_level_modifications.input: Provide Modification1-4: Low, Middle, or High
ability_level_modifications.output: Use Activities for Adaptations1-4 to change activity according to teacher request for child ability level. Revise lesson plan with modified teacher script

example_high_level.description: Children are given two previously learned sounds at a time; they must add in the target sound (either beginning, middle, or end) to create a word
example_high_level.teacher_script: Great! Now we are going to play our Sound Puzzle +Level: High. We are listening for the /z/ sound at the beginning of the word. The /z/ sound is going to be the beginning sound of the word. Each of you has the /z/ sound in in front of you. I am going to give you two sounds. These are sounds you already know. You are going to put the /z/ sound and the two sounds I give you together to make a word, and it could be a nonsense word. Watch me. I will show you first. Here's two sounds: /a/ and /p/. I am thinking about ordering the sounds to make a word. I am going to place /z/ first, than /a/, then /p/. {teacher sound out the phonemes /z/ /a/ /p/}. When I say go, tell me your word. So, you would say: zap. My turn. Your two sounds are /i/ and /p/. Put them in order. Get Ready...Go. (children should say zip). {Teacher repeats this process to cement sound to memory then connects to letter form}
